questions.q: What real Snowflake feature did Lessons 3-4 cover?
options: Semi-structured JSON ingestion into a VARIANT column, then parsing with :field::type syntax
Setting up a new Snowflake account from scratch
Writing Python stored procedures
Configuring Snowflake's billing and credit alerts
questions.explain: Lessons 3-4 built the raw JSON ingestion pipeline and the real VARIANT parsing syntax used throughout the rest of the chapter.

questions.q: What distinguished the two Tasks built in Lessons 6-7?
options: One was an idempotent upsert for current-state data; the other was an append-only, non-idempotent log for event data
One used Python, the other used SQL
One ran every hour, the other ran every second
They were identical in every respect
questions.explain: ticket_facts_sync_task's upsert MERGE was idempotent; finance_refund_task's append-only MERGE was not — a distinction that turned out to matter directly in Lessons 13-15.

questions.q: What does this lesson say Lessons 13-15 were really about, beyond MERGE statements and TASK_HISTORY syntax?
options: A transferable diagnostic habit: reproduce, isolate, confirm with a real tool, then fix the root cause
Memorizing every Information Schema function Snowflake offers
Learning to avoid Streams and Tasks entirely in future projects
A one-time fix specific to this exact scenario, with no broader lesson
questions.explain: The diagnostic process — reproduce, isolate, confirm, fix the root cause — is the actual transferable skill, more than the specific SQL involved.

questions.q: How does this chapter's scope compare honestly to the existing Advanced capstone?
options: This chapter stayed narrower on purpose — one Snowflake-native pipeline, no external orchestrator — to cover Streams and Tasks in real depth
This chapter covers strictly more ground than the Advanced capstone in every respect
The two capstones are unrelated and use different fictional companies
This chapter replaces the need to ever build the Advanced capstone
questions.explain: The Advanced capstone adds dbt, Airflow, Terraform, and CI/CD; this chapter deliberately stayed narrower to focus on Streams and Tasks specifically.

questions.q: What does this lesson suggest doing if you've already built the Advanced capstone?
options: Revisit its Streams/Tasks-adjacent lessons with this chapter's bug fresh in mind, since the overlapping-execution risk applies anywhere a Stream has more than one consumer
Delete the Advanced capstone's content, since this chapter supersedes it
Nothing — the two projects have no meaningful connection
Rebuild the Advanced capstone's RBAC policies from scratch
questions.explain: The diagnostic insight from this chapter's bug generalizes beyond this specific scenario, including to the Advanced capstone's own Streams/Tasks content.
